26 days later and I'm still not over it. 🧡

Click-a-thon 2026 was @Cli@clickhouse.inc's first ever in-person hackathon in India, and what a way to start. 70 teams. 206 builders. 24 hours of shipping, debugging, and running on chai and pure adrenaline.

I've run a lot of community events over the years, but there's something about watching a room full of builders refuse to sleep because their demo isn't quite right yet. That energy doesn't fade. Clearly, since I'm still posting about it almost a month later.

To everyone who built, mentored, judged, and cheered: you made this one unforgettable. The bar is set. Now we raise it.

See you at the next one. 🚀

text:
Spent a few days last week at #VibeCon hosted by @Replit in #NewYork, and I left thinking less about what AI can build and more about what we should build with it.
The event mixed product, AI and creativity in a way that felt different. Builders weren't just talking about speed and agents. They were talking about taste, meaning, emotion and intention. And two panels captured that shift perfectly.

Creativity, Taste and Meaning in the Age of AI, with Michele Catasta and Meaghan Choi from @AnthropicAI 
The idea that stayed with me:
"Taste is not polish. Taste is discernment."
Because when almost anything can be built, the real value moves from execution to judgment. Taste is not the final visual layer. It starts much earlier: the problem you choose, the user you understand, the features you remove, the things you decide not to build at all. Building is getting easier. 
Choosing well is getting harder.

Everyone's a creative. Now what?, the closing conversation between Amjad Masad and spi

Open Source it is. Which is strongly engraved into the culture of Polaris.

This year, 18 Polaris students became part of that culture through Google Summer of Code 2026.

author.name: Shweta Rajpal Kohli
author.description: President & CEO, Startup Policy Forum (SPF); Bridging innovation and policy ecosystems; ex Sequoia Capital, Peak XV, Uber, Salesforce, NDTV

text:
🎬‼️ The teaser dropped last week. Now the full episode. Mukund Jha, founder of Emergent, arguably among the fastest-growing AI companies in the world right now, joined us on IndiaAI in Action, a special series of Startup Policy Forum, in collaboration with IndiaAI Mission. 

We spent time with Mukund at Vibecon, Emergent's blockbuster hackathon that saw 25,000 applicants compete for 300 spots, with the winner walking away with a Y Combinator interview. The energy at the venue - Polaris School of Technology - said everything about where Indian AI is headed.

Here's what we covered:

➡️ The AI opportunity: global and India. Mukund's take is unequivocal: we are underhyped. The transformation coming from new AI companies will be “magical.” Software that once cost $1M to build now costs $10K. India's edge? The largest population, a data advantage, and an application layer wide open for the taking. His advice: building global is as hard as building for India. So you might as well think big.

The energy was crazy. 
A room full of participants team, i was amazed to see what they were building & demos.

Top 10 presented their work. 3 won. ✌️

There were CEOs, board members, founders, creators and industry leaders in the same room to network. 💯

One can learn so much in a few hours at these events. It exposes you to the technology in real world and tells you what’s happening on ground.
